title: Shift equations of the three comparisons in the twisted pullback square
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a fixed algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$; finite coefficient fields range over its actual finite intermediate fields, and every inclusion may be an equality. Write $\mathcal C_R(W)$ for the framework raw rational constructible category and its common integral constructible objects. All schemes occurring in a framework pullback or Tate twist have $\ell$ invertible in their residue fields; whenever PBC coordinates are used, assume the scheme is Noetherian of finite Krull dimension with $\ell$ invertible in its stalks. All maps between schemes are arbitrary unless smoothness is expressly specified; shifts are by integers and $d\in\mathbf N$. Use the finite-field and coefficient conventions of [def-pur-conventions], the Cartesian-square convention of [def-pc-base-change], the raw rational category of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], the specified derived pullback and tensor of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], the exact scalar functors and comparisons of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], the integral-normalized pullback comparisons of [def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange], and the ordinary adic source scalar comparison of [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality]. For component isomorphisms w:F→G and specified coherent shift structures on F and G, define ShiftNatural by w_{K[n]} followed by the G shift comparison equals the F shift comparison followed by w_K[n], for every integer n and object K. SquareShiftEquations for the four-arrow square means ShiftNatural for z_u, t and m at every finite coefficient field, using exactly the pullback shifts and the D shifts from ShiftCoherence and their specified composites. Together with the seven coefficient-family shift equations this fixes the shift identifications of (Z), (C) and (M), with line degree zero and common even shift 2d. Use the normalized constructions of [def-pur-twisted-pullback-shift-coherence].
